name.en: Fake DVLA message: “update your details” or “claim your vehicle tax refund”

how.en: A text or email says it is from the DVLA. It may say your details must be updated or your driving licence could be affected, or that you are due a vehicle tax refund. A link leads to a copycat site that steals personal and payment details. The DVLA never asks for bank details or to confirm payment details, and vehicle tax refunds are paid automatically.

text.en: A text or email says it is from the DVLA.
It says your licence could be affected, or that you are owed a refund.
It gives a link to update your details or claim the money.
The site asks for your bank or card details.
DVLA: Your driving licence information is out of date. Update your details today to avoid your licence being suspended: [link]
DVLA: You are entitled to a vehicle tax refund of £84.50. Confirm your payment details to receive it: [link]

en: A vehicle tax refund offered by email or text: refunds are automatic.
A threat to your driving licence with a link.
Any site other than GOV.UK for DVLA services.
Don’t click the link. Use only GOV.UK for DVLA services.
Report the email or text to the NCSC (forward texts to 7726) and delete it.
If you paid or gave card details, call your bank straight away (you can dial 159).
